fullPassage:
Today, I'm looking for a tiny animal that's hiding in one of Europe's most beautiful capital cities, Vienna. Now it's home to nearly 2 million people, but 50% of the city is green space. What I'm looking for is probably one of Europe's most critically endangered mammals.
Now, I've come really early to a graveyard to try to see some hamsters because this is one of the best times of day to see them. At this time of the day, there's nobody around so they don't have to avoid people while looking for food. These little ones have been in the area for decades, but now live among the dead because development has robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit.
Look! I just found one over there. See how it is trying to stuff its cheeks full? Hamsters can pack a quarter of their body weight inside their cheeks, which helps them get through the winter. Surprisingly, they not only feed on nuts and flowers, but have also adapted to eating candle wax, which is a good source of fat and is easy to find in graveyards.
Even though the hamsters here have adapted to the noises of the city, they still keep a watchful eye, as predators are never too far away. They may need to quickly escape back down into their holes, which are complex structures stretching under the ground. Despite urban areas generally having a negative effect on wildlife, cities can actually provide islands of protection for it.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그것의(its) 볼을 가득 채우려 하고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ it's → its: 소유격 its(그것의)가 맞음. it's = it is(축약형). 'its cheeks'(그것의 볼)

❌ ② feed: 'they feed on' 복수 주어에 원형. 정상
✅ ④ finding → to find: 'be easy to find'에서 to부정사 사용. 형용사 + to부정사 구문. finding은 불가

det.korean: 야생동물을 위해 보호의 섬을 제공한다. 원문은 it(= wildlife, 단수)이지 them(복수)이 아니다.

❌ ① they: 대명사. 'the green fields they used to inhabit'에서 they = hamsters. 정상
❌ ② which: 관계대명사 계속적 용법. 앞 절 전체를 받음. 정상
❌ ③ Despite: 전치사. 'Despite + 동명사구' 정상
det.tip: wildlife(야생동물)는 불가산 명사 → 단수 대명사 it으로 받음. them(복수)은 불가

❌ ② neutral(중립적인): 역접의 강도가 부족
❌ ④ permanent(영구적인): 긍정/부정 방향성 부재
det.tip: Despite A, B: A(부정적)에도 불구하고 B(보호 제공). 역접 관계에서 A에 들어갈 단어는 B와 반대 방향

questions.passage: Today, I'm looking for a tiny animal that's hiding in one of Europe's most beautiful capital cities, Vienna. Now it's home to nearly 2 million people, but 50% of the city is green space. What I'm looking for is probably one of Europe's most critically endangered mammals. Now, I've come really early to a graveyard to try to see some hamsters because this is one of the best times of day to see them. At this time of the day, there's nobody around so they don't have to avoid people while looking for food. These little ones have been in the area for decades, but now live among the dead because development has robbed them of the green fields they used to inhabit. Look!
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 이른 아침에 묘지를 방문한 이유로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이른 아침이 햄스터를 보기 가장 좋은 시간이기 때문이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 관찰하기 좋은 시간: 'this is one of the best times of day to see them' — 직접 이유
❌ ① 야경: 이른 아침이므로 야경과 무관
❌ ② 먹이 주기: 먹이를 주는 것이 아닌 관찰
❌ ③ 개발 조사: 개발 조사가 아닌 동물 관찰
det.tip: because = 이유를 나타내는 접속사. 'this is one of the best times' = 가장 좋은 시간 중 하나
